4.3 Tasks/Routines/Functions 
The analog inputs and outputs will be scaled wi th MapIn and MapOut routines as described 
according to the MCCPDC Controller Guidelin es document and using the values in the 
MCCPDC Alarms Hard Soft IO Listing.xlsx.  For this work the following sp ecific routines are expected: 
 R105_EMS  R110_MapInLAD  R111_MapInFBD  R120_MapOutLAD  R121_MapOutFBD 
4.4 Operator Interface 
Each of the EMS input signals is displayed in  engineering units on th e HMI.  As mentioned 
previously, with the proper credentials, the input points can be simulated for calibration or other 
maintenance activities.  Similarly, given the pr oper credentials, the alarm limits for the EMS 
signals are also available for revi ew and adjustment  via the HMI. 
The visual and audible annunciators  (light trees and audible aler ts) also provide feedback to 
personnel in the area without the need to actively view an HMI screen.   
4.5 Messages and Alarming 
The EMS messages and alarms, together with other system alarms, are de scribed in the overall 
PCS system document named MCCPDC PCS-CP01 Al arms Hard Soft IO Listing.xlsx.  That 
document provides, among other de tails, the alarm text, the input point tag identifier, the alarm 
setpoint, and any time-delay associated with the alarm.  For the alarms listed here, alarm limit 
processing, time delay, etc. is handled in the PL C and not in the FactoryTalk Alarm and Events 
Server.  The alarm setpoints are not calcu lated but are static, user-adjus table values via the HMI as 
detailed in the MCCPDC PCS-CP01 Alarms  Hard Soft IO Listing.xlsx document. 
 See Section 4.1.6.1 Alarms/Beacons to see the de scription of acknowledging and resetting of 
alarms.
